data.why: The repo ships no example audio or segmentation file; a segmentation .txt in the documented 'time<TAB>New Point' format was synthesized, and a byte-identical copy was pre-placed server-side because the onsets upload callback (app.py, set_class_instance) only reads the uploaded file's name, then opens 'assets/<name>' on disk instead of using the uploaded bytes.

goals: Import an audio excerpt with its hand-made temporal segmentation and compute static harmonic descriptors (roughness, harmonicity, inverse harmonicity) describing each isolated chord (verticality)
Import several separated audio tracks for the same excerpt to unlock concordance and total concordance descriptors that need per-voice spectra
Compute dynamic descriptors (harmonic change, differential concordance, differential roughness) to characterize the transitions between consecutive chords
Plot two chosen descriptors against each other on an interactive 2D map, as points or as trajectories, to compare the harmonic profile of a passage
Overlay and compare the harmonic trajectories of several distinct musical excerpts on the same descriptor map
Tune signal-processing parameters (CQT pitch range, analysis window, HPSS percussive filtering) to refine which spectral content the descriptors are computed from

review.summary: The goal and the input-side phases match the README well, labels are clean, and most cited screens show what the nodes claim. But no audio was available, so nothing was computed and the map was never seen. Without that results stage the tree covers only setup, and it needs a re-run with real audio plus the structural fixes listed before filing.
